meta.title: Netball Umpiring Handbook — Ruling Knowledge Base
meta.source: World Netball — Rules of Netball, 2024 Edition
meta.sourceNote: Grounded verbatim in the 2024 edition. Where English wording diverges across translations, the English text is authoritative (Foreword). This knowledge base is a decision-support aid for umpires, not a substitute for the full rulebook.
meta.disclaimer: Always apply umpire judgement. Player safety is the paramount consideration in every decision.

signals.name: Start / restart of play
signals.how: Arm held high, angled towards goal end of team with centre pass.

signals.name: Hold time
signals.how: Facing timekeeper, one hand vertical and other horizontal to form a 'T'.

signals.name: Direction of pass
signals.how: Arm outstretched to side, pointing to goal end of team with the pass (for centre pass, sanction or action).

signals.name: Throw-in (goal line)
signals.how: Arm angled down, pointing to base of goalpost, for attacking team at its goal end.

signals.name: Advantage
signals.how: Arm sweeps across body towards goal end of team with advantage.

signals.name: Possession
signals.how: Hands, palms inward a short distance apart, in a catching motion.

signals.name: Goal scored
signals.how: Arm held vertically.

signals.name: Goal not scored
signals.how: Arms move from side to side across each other above the waist.

signals.name: Centre positioned incorrectly
signals.how: Hand traces a horizontal circle.

signals.name: Incorrect position or incorrect use of court areas
signals.how: Hand traces a medium upward arc in the direction of the incorrect position or area. Used for offside, breaking, over a third, untouched centre pass, not set, preventing re-entry, defending from out of court, leaving the court, incorrect throw-in and incorrect shot.

signals.name: Interference with shot or intimidation
signals.how: Hand traces a small arc in front of the face.

signals.name: Tactical change
signals.how: Circular motion of both forearms around each other above the waist.

signals.name: Held ball
signals.how: Arm held vertically with three fingers displayed.

signals.name: Repossession
signals.how: Hands, palms inward a short distance apart, twist from side to side in a parallel motion.

signals.name: Incorrect playing of the ball
signals.how: One hand, palm down, moves vertically up and down in a bouncing action. Also for playing ball on ground, using the goalpost, replayed ball.

signals.name: Short pass
signals.how: Hands, palms inward a short distance apart, one hand moves towards the other held stationary.

signals.name: Footwork
signals.how: Hands, palms down, move vertically up and down in opposite directions.

signals.name: Obstruction (player in possession of the ball)
signals.how: Hands, palms inward, held a short distance apart.

signals.name: Obstruction (player not in possession of the ball)
signals.how: Arms angled out from body below the waist.

signals.name: Contact
signals.how: Hand, palm facing down, taps opposite forearm.

signals.name: Warning
signals.how: Arms crossed above head.

signals.name: Suspension
signals.how: Arm held vertically with two fingers displayed.

signals.name: Ordering off
signals.how: Hand sweeps from player towards their team bench.

free.label: Free pass
free.note: May be taken by any player allowed in the area. A player taking a free pass may not shoot for goal [6.3].

penalty.label: Penalty pass
penalty.note: The infringer must stand out of play beside the player taking it, and not move or take any part in play (including verbal comments) until the ball is released [6.4]. A GS/GA taking a penalty pass in the goal circle may pass or shoot [6.6].

throwin.label: Throw-in
throwin.note: Taken from outside the court with at least one foot within 15 cm of the line at the point indicated [6.11].

possession.label: Possession
possession.note: Awarded where the ball was when play stopped; any player allowed in the area may take it [6.15–6.17].

rulings.title: Footwork — moving the landing foot illegally
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Landing foot lifted and regrounded before the ball is released
Dragging or sliding the landing foot
Hopping on either foot
Jumping from both feet and landing on both feet while still holding the ball
procedure: Identify the landing foot: for a one-foot landing it is the foot first grounded; for a two-foot landing it is the foot not moved first [Definitions].
A player may step with the second foot in any direction and may pivot on the landing foot, but must pass or shoot before regrounding the lifted landing foot [13.1–13.2].
Penalise if the player drags/slides the landing foot, hops, or jumps from both feet to land on both feet while still in possession [13.3].
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 17.
rulings.notes: The foot placed at the point indicated for any sanction/action is treated as a 'one-foot landing' [6.19]. At a centre pass the landing-foot rules in [8.12] apply.
rulings.heading: Other foot movements
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Held ball — not released within three seconds
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Player in possession does not pass or shoot within three seconds
Applies equally to the centre pass [8.13] and to a shot at goal [9.6b]
procedure: Count three seconds from the moment the player gains clear possession.
A player in possession must pass or shoot within three seconds [11.4].
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 13 (arm vertical, three fingers).
For a shooter, the same three-second limit applies from catching the ball [9.6b].
rulings.notes: The Centre taking the centre pass must also release within three seconds [8.13].
rulings.heading: While in possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Short pass — no space to intercept
rulings.position: Free pass where the ball is caught/touched by the receiving player of the same team.
keyIndicators: No room for an opponent to defend, deflect or intercept between passer and receiver
Two team-mates gaining possession in quick succession, second finishing with the ball [12.2]
procedure: Judge whether there was sufficient space for an opposing player to deflect or intercept the ball as it travelled [12.1].
If not, award a free pass where the receiving team-mate caught or touched the ball.
For two team-mates gaining possession in quick succession, the first must keep the ball; if the second finishes with it, rule short pass [12.2].
Give hand signal 16.
rulings.notes: This is about space for a contest, not a fixed distance — contrast with the 0.9 m obstruction distance.
rulings.heading: Short pass
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Over a third — ball not touched in each third
rulings.position: Free pass taken by the transverse line where the ball first entered the third incorrectly. If the ball goes out of court over the goal line, a throw-in is awarded instead.
keyIndicators: Ball travels over a complete third without being caught or touched in it
Player astride the transverse line — pass must be taken in one of those two thirds [12.6]
procedure: The ball must be caught or touched by a player in each third [12.3].
The receiver must be wholly in the third, or land with the first foot / both feet wholly in that third [12.4].
Award a free pass by the transverse line where the ball first entered the third incorrectly and give hand signal 10.
If the ball instead goes out over the goal line, award a throw-in [12.4].
rulings.notes: After catching correctly a player may step into an adjacent third; any subsequent pass is deemed made from where they first landed [12.5].
keywords: not touched in the middle third
rulings.heading: Over a third
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Offside — player in an area not designated for their position
rulings.position: Free pass where the player entered the offside area.
keyIndicators: Player enters a court area not allowed for their playing position, with or without the ball
Not offside if a body part is in contact with (but not over) the line bounding their own area
procedure: Confirm the player's position and permitted areas [3.10–3.11].
A player is offside when they enter an area not designated for their position, whether or not they touch the ball [14.1].

Exception: entering solely to retrieve a ball to set a sanction/action is not offside [6.20], and a player may reach across/lean into an offside area if they make no contact with the ground there [14.3].
Award a free pass where the player entered the offside area and give hand signal 10.
If two opposing players go offside, one before the other, penalise the first [14.2]. If simultaneous and neither touches the ball, play on [20.3].
rulings.notes: See the position/area chart: GS 1-2, GA 1-2-3, WA 2-3, C 2-3-4, WD 3-4, GD 3-4-5, GK 4-5.
rulings.heading: Requirements
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Contact — unfair physical interference with an opponent
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless this disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the contacted player was standing).
keyIndicators: Pushing, tripping, grabbing, holding or leaning on an opponent
Knocking/hitting an opponent, including when shooting
Placing hand(s) on a ball held by an opponent
Contact must cause loss of ball, interference with a passing/shooting action, or a change in body position that unfairly disadvantages the opponent [17.2]
procedure: Determine whether physical contact occurred and whether it unfairly interfered with the opponent's play [17.1].
Penalise only if it caused one of the [17.2] outcomes — otherwise it is fair contest and is not penalised [17.3].
Award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing (or where the contacted player was, if that avoids disadvantage), and give hand signal 20.
The infringer stands out of play until the ball is released [6.4].
If the contact endangers safety (especially head/neck), treat as dangerous play and apply a game management action [17.9], [19.11].
rulings.notes: Incidental contact that does not cause interference is fair contest [17.3]. Head/neck contact must never be given advantage [7.4c].
keywords: hit the ball out of her hands
knocked the ball out of her hands
hit it out of her hands
hit the ball from her hands
knocked it out of her hands
hit the ball out of the hands
rulings.heading: Interference
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Obstruction — defending within 0.9 m of a player with the ball
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless this disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the obstructed player was standing).
keyIndicators: Defender less than 0.9 m (3 ft) from the landing foot of the player with the ball while attempting to defend, deflect or intercept
Distance measured on the ground from the landing foot to the defender's nearer foot
procedure: Measure 0.9 m on the ground from the nearest part of the landing foot of the player with the ball to the defender's nearer foot [16.1].
A defender closer than 0.9 m may not attempt to defend, deflect or intercept, and may not use arms/movements that interfere with the passing or shooting action [16.7].
If the shooter/passer reduces the distance, or the defender jumped from a legal distance without interfering, it is not obstruction [16.6].
Award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing and give hand signal 18. The infringer stands out of play [6.4].
rulings.notes: If the player with the ball pivots, the defender must adjust to remain 0.9 m from where the landing foot is now grounded [16.5]. A defender within 0.9 m may stand still with no defending effort — that is not obstruction [16.7].
keywords: too close to the player with the ball
rulings.heading: Player in possession of the ball
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Obstruction — using arms to prevent an opponent's movement (no ball)
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless this disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the obstructed player was standing).
keyIndicators: Within 0.9 m of an opponent who does not have the ball, using arm movements away from the body to prevent that opponent's movement
Not permitted except as required for natural body stance
procedure: A player within 0.9 m of an opponent may stretch arms only to catch/deflect/intercept a pass or rebound, or to momentarily signal for a pass [16.8].
They may not use movements that take the arms away from the body to prevent an opponent's movement, except for natural body stance [16.9].
Award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing and give hand signal 19.
rulings.notes: Distinguish from obstruction of a player in possession (signal 18). Here the opponent does not have the ball.
rulings.heading: Player not in possession of the ball
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Out of court — ball goes out over a line
rulings.position: Throw-in to the team that did NOT touch the ball last on court, taken in line with where the ball went out.
keyIndicators: Ball touches the ground, an object, or a person outside the court
A court player holds the ball while it is in contact with something outside the court
Ball is NOT out if it hits the goalpost and rebounds in, or lands on but not over a line
procedure: Decide which team last touched the ball while on court [15.1].
Award a throw-in to the opposing team, taken in line with where the ball crossed the line.
A whistle is only required if it is not clear that the ball is out [4.6e].
Note: the ball is not out if it rebounds off any part of the goalpost into court, or lands on but not over a line [15.4].
rulings.notes: A ball from a centre pass may not go untouched over the side line bounding the centre third — throw-in [8.15].
rulings.heading: Ball out of court
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Out of court — player lands or stands outside the court with the ball
rulings.position: Throw-in to the team that did NOT catch/touch the ball, in line with where the player landed or is standing outside the court.
keyIndicators: Player catches the ball in the air and lands wholly or partly outside the court
Player catches/touches the ball while standing partly inside and partly outside the court
procedure: A player is not out of court if a body part is on but not over a line [15.5].
A player may jump from inside and pass or shoot before landing outside [15.6].
If the player lands or stands outside while playing the ball, award a throw-in to the opposing team in line with that point [15.3].
A player partly/wholly in the court surround must re-enter with no surround contact before playing the ball [15.8].
rulings.notes: A player leaving the field of play without the umpire's permission is treated as a late player [15.9], [3.8].
rulings.heading: Player outside the court
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Leaving the court — moving out to gain advantage
rulings.position: Penalty pass taken on court in line with where the infringer was standing.
keyIndicators: A player with no contact with the ball moves into the court surround for a reason other than repositioning back onto the court
procedure: A player with no ball contact may move into the court surround only to reposition back onto the court [15.7].
If they leave for any other reason (e.g. to gain space or advantage), award a penalty pass on court in line with where they were standing.
Give hand signal 10.
rulings.notes: Distinguish from 'defending from out of court' [15.10], which is a separate penalty.
rulings.heading: Player outside the court
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Defending from out of court
rulings.position: Penalty pass taken on court near to where the infringer was standing.
keyIndicators: A player standing outside the court attempts to defend a player on the court (with or without the ball)
procedure: A player standing outside the court may not attempt to defend an on-court player, whether or not that player has the ball [15.10].
Award a penalty pass on court near where the infringer was standing and give hand signal 10.
keywords: arms in from out of court
rulings.heading: Defending from out of court
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Incorrect throw-in
rulings.position: Throw-in to the opposing team (from the same position, or where the infringement occurred).
keyIndicators: Thrower does not stand outside with a foot within 15 cm of the line at the indicated point
Thrower steps on/over the line before releasing, or the ball fails to enter the court
Thrower steps behind an offside area while holding the ball
procedure: The thrower stands outside the court with at least one foot within 15 cm of the line at the point indicated (this is the landing foot) [6.11].
They may not step on the lines/court until the ball is released; the ball must enter the court [6.13–6.14].
For a foot-fault or ball not entering, award a throw-in to the opposing team from the same position; for stepping behind an offside area, throw-in where the infringement occurred [6.11].
Give hand signal 10.
rulings.notes: Throwing over a third: free pass in the third where the ball entered incorrectly [6.12]. From the goal line the ball must go into the goal third; from the side line into the nearest or adjacent third.
rulings.heading: Conditions for throw-in
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Playing the ball on the ground
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Falling on the ball to gain possession
Gaining possession while lying, sitting or kneeling on the ground
Passing or shooting while lying, sitting or kneeling [11.8d]
procedure: A player may not fall on the ball, nor gain possession while lying/sitting/kneeling [11.2].
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 15.
rulings.notes: Rolling the ball to oneself to gain possession is allowed [11.1b]; rolling the ball to another player is not [11.8c].
rulings.heading: Gaining possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Using the goalpost as a support
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Player uses the goalpost as a support, including to gain or retain possession or balance
procedure: A player may not use the goalpost as a support, including to gain or retain possession [11.3].
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 15.
rulings.notes: A defender must not cause the goalpost to move to interfere with a shot — that is interference with the shot, a penalty pass [9.7a].
rulings.heading: Gaining possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Repossession — touching the ball again after releasing it
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: After releasing the ball, a player touches it again before another player touches it or it rebounds from the goalpost
procedure: After having possession and releasing the ball, a player may not touch it again before another player touches it or it rebounds from the goalpost [11.6].
This includes a dropped ball retrieved by the same player, or catching one's own missed shot before anyone else touches it (a shot rebounding off the post may be caught [11.1c]).
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 14.
rulings.notes: Contrast 'replayed ball' [11.7], which is about a player who never had full possession.
rulings.heading: While in possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Replayed ball — illegal repeated play without possession
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Without gaining full possession, a player bats or bounces the ball more than the permitted once before passing it on
Gaining possession then batting/bouncing to another player
procedure: Without possession a player may bat once, or bounce once, then bat/bounce to another player, or touch it in an uncontrolled manner then bat/bounce it on [11.7].
Exceeding this (e.g. batting the ball twice to control it, then passing) is a replayed ball.
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 15.
rulings.notes: A player may touch the ball in an uncontrolled manner once or more and then catch it [11.1f] — that is legal gaining of possession, not a replayed ball.
rulings.heading: Without having possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Incorrect playing of the ball — kick, fist, roll to another
rulings.position: Free pass where the infringement occurred.
keyIndicators: Kicking the ball
Striking the ball with a fist
Rolling the ball to another player
Passing or shooting while lying, sitting or kneeling on the ground
procedure: A player may not kick the ball, strike it with a fist, roll it to another player, or pass/shoot while lying/sitting/kneeling [11.8].
Award a free pass where the infringement occurred and give hand signal 15.
rulings.notes: Rolling the ball to oneself to gain possession is permitted [11.1b]; deliberately kicking is not (an unintentional touch with the foot in gaining possession may be an uncontrolled touch [11.1f]).
rulings.heading: Prohibited actions
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Breaking — entering the centre third before the whistle
rulings.position: Free pass in the centre third by the transverse line where the player entered the centre third.
keyIndicators: A player (other than the two Centres) enters the centre third before the whistle to start play
procedure: Apart from both Centres, no player may enter the centre third until the whistle is blown to start play [8.11].
Award a free pass in the centre third by the transverse line where the player entered, and give hand signal 10.
If two opposing players break simultaneously and neither touches the ball, play on; if one touches the ball, award possession to the team who last had it [20.1d], [20.2].
rulings.notes: This is the most common centre-pass infringement — watch the WA/GA and WD/GD on the transverse lines.
rulings.heading: Position of players
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Centre pass — incorrect position
rulings.position: Free pass at the relevant point (centre circle, or on court near where the player was positioned incorrectly).
keyIndicators: The passing Centre does not have at least one foot wholly in the centre circle [8.8]
The opposing Centre is not in the centre third [8.9]
Any player is not positioned in their correct third when play is due to start [8.10]
procedure: The Centre in possession stands with at least one foot wholly within the centre circle [8.8] — free pass in the centre circle if not (signal 9 for the Centre).
The opposing Centre must be in the centre third and free to move [8.9] — free pass in the goal third by the transverse line if not.
Other players must be on court and in their correct thirds when play is due to start [8.10] — free pass on court near the incorrect position (signal 10).
Blow for the centre pass first, then blow again to penalise the infringement [8.6].
rulings.notes: Use signal 9 (horizontal circle) specifically for the Centre positioned incorrectly; signal 10 for other players.
keywords: not in their third at centre
rulings.heading: Position of players
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Centre pass — footwork out of the circle
rulings.position: Free pass in the centre circle.
keyIndicators: The Centre breaks the footwork rule when stepping out of the centre circle after the whistle
procedure: When the whistle starts play the Centre may step out of the circle but must obey the footwork rule [8.12].
If only one foot was wholly inside the circle, that is the landing foot; if both were inside, the foot not moved first is the landing foot.
Penalise footwork with a free pass in the centre circle and give hand signal 17.
rulings.heading: Controlling the centre pass
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Centre pass — untouched / caught in the goal third
rulings.position: Free pass in the goal third by the transverse line where the player was in contact with the ground in the goal third (or near where they landed out of court).
keyIndicators: A centre pass is not caught/touched by a player wholly within, or landing first/both feet within, the centre third [8.14]
A player from the passing team catches it in the goal third, lands astride the transverse line, or lands out of court [8.16]
procedure: The centre pass must be touched or caught by a player standing wholly in, or landing with the first/both feet wholly in, the centre third [8.14].
If not, award a free pass in the goal third by the transverse line where the player was in the goal third, and give hand signal 10.
If an opposing player catches it in the goal third or lands astride the line, the umpire may apply advantage [8.17].
rulings.notes: The ball from a centre pass may not go untouched over the side line bounding the centre third — throw-in [8.15].
rulings.heading: Controlling the centre pass
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Interference with shot
rulings.position: Penalty pass. If the shot is successful, the goal is scored as well.
keyIndicators: A defender causes the goalpost to move to interfere with a shot
A defender deflects the ball on its downward flight towards the ring, including touching it up through the net
procedure: A defending player may not move the goalpost to interfere with a shot, or deflect a ball on its downward flight towards the ring [9.7].
Award a penalty pass and give hand signal 11. If the shot was nonetheless successful, the goal still counts.
At the end of a period this may extend time for the penalty pass [9.2], [2.3].
rulings.notes: A legal deflection that then goes through the ring still scores a goal [9.3].
rulings.heading: Taking a shot
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Incorrect shot — contact with ground outside the goal circle
rulings.position: Free pass where the player made physical contact with the ground outside the goal circle. No goal is scored.
keyIndicators: GS/GA has physical contact with the ground outside the goal circle while catching, touching or shooting
procedure: In taking a shot the player must have no physical contact with the ground outside the goal circle, including while catching or touching the ball [9.6a].
They may lean on the ball, roll it, or pick it up from the goal third outside the circle, provided no ground contact outside the circle.
If infringed, award a free pass where the ground contact occurred; no goal is scored. Give hand signal 10.
rulings.notes: The shooter must also shoot within three seconds [9.6b] (held ball) and obey footwork [9.6c].
rulings.heading: Taking a shot
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Shooting from a free pass
rulings.position: Free pass and no goal is scored.
keyIndicators: A GS/GA shoots directly from a free pass awarded in the goal circle
procedure: A player taking a free pass may not shoot for goal [6.3].
If they shoot, no goal is scored and a free pass is awarded to the opposing team.
Terminology: 'Shooting from free pass'.
rulings.notes: Contrast a penalty pass in the circle, where a GS/GA may pass OR shoot [6.6].
rulings.heading: Conditions for free pass
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Participating — infringer not standing out of play at a penalty
rulings.position: A further penalty pass, which may be advanced [18.17].
keyIndicators: The infringer does not move quickly to the indicated spot, or moves/talks/takes part before the ball is released
The infringer attempts to intercept a penalty pass the taker plays immediately [6.7b]
procedure: At a penalty pass the infringer must stand beside but away from the taker, and not move or take any part in play (including verbal comments) until the ball is released [6.4].
If they participate, award a further penalty pass (which may be advanced [18.17]).
Terminology: 'Participating'.
rulings.notes: If the taker chooses to play immediately before the sanction is set, the infringer still may not take part or attempt to intercept [6.7].
keywords: did not stand out of play
rulings.heading: Conditions for penalty pass
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Not set — sanction taken from the wrong position
rulings.position: Re-take from the correct position (free pass if on court; throw-in if off court).
keyIndicators: The player taking a sanction/action is not correctly positioned with the ball before playing it
For a penalty pass, the infringer is also not yet correctly positioned
procedure: A sanction/action is 'set' once the taker is correctly positioned with the ball (and, for a penalty, the infringer is correctly positioned) [Definitions].
If the ball is played before it is set, penalise 'Not set': free pass (on court) or throw-in (off court) [6.2].
Give hand signal 10.
rulings.notes: A player correctly positioned may choose to play the ball before the sanction is set [6.7]; the umpire may call 'taken' sparingly to clarify [6.7a].
rulings.heading: Conditions for all sanctions and actions
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Dangerous play
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringement occurred. Player is suspended, or ordered off in a serious case. Always order off for intentional or highly reckless dangerous play.
keyIndicators: Any unnecessarily forceful, careless, reckless or dangerous action affecting another player's safety
Especially any head and/or neck contact, or head/neck contact with the playing enclosure including the goalpost
procedure: Hold time and award a penalty pass where the infringement occurred [19.11].

Apply a game management action: the player must be suspended (signal 22), or ordered off (signal 23) in a serious case; always order off for intentional or highly reckless dangerous play [18.29], [18.37].
Weigh intent, impact, speed, force, and whether stationary or moving [19.12].
Advantage must never be applied to dangerous play or head/neck contact [7.4].
rulings.notes: A warning is not sufficient for dangerous play — the minimum game management action is suspension. Player safety is paramount [18.5].
rulings.heading: Dangerous play
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Unsporting behaviour (incl. retaliation, abuse)
rulings.terminology: Unsporting behaviour (retaliation / abusive behaviour / actions contrary to good sporting behaviour)
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringement occurred. The player is warned or suspended; in a serious case, ordered off.
keyIndicators: Retaliation to an opponent's actions [19.8]
Offensive, insulting or abusive language or gestures [19.9]
Any action adding hostility or contrary to good sporting behaviour or the image of the game [19.7], [19.10]
procedure: Award a penalty pass where the infringement occurred [19.7].
A warning MUST be given for all instances of unsporting behaviour [18.25] — signal 21; escalate to suspension (signal 22) or, in a serious case, ordering off (signal 23).
Never apply advantage to unsporting behaviour [7.4a].
rulings.notes: Retaliation is penalised even if the opponent infringed first [19.8]. Deal firmly and calmly; do not criticise or coach [18.1].
rulings.heading: Unsporting behaviour
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Unfair play (delaying, intentional/repeated infringing, disputed ruling, intimidation)
rulings.terminology: Specific description of unfair play (delaying play / intentional infringing / repeated infringing / disputed ruling / intimidation)
rulings.position: Penalty pass which is advanced.
keyIndicators: Delaying play or wasting time [19.2]
Intentional infringing [19.3] or repeated infringing by a player or team [19.4]
Disputing an umpire's ruling [19.5]
Intimidation — covering eyes, swiping the ball at the face, loud/sudden noises, stomping, waving arms, sledging [19.6]
procedure: Award a penalty pass which is advanced [19.1], using the specific terminology for the type of unfair play.
For intimidation, use hand signal 11 (small arc in front of the face).
Repeated infringing follows from a player being spoken to more than once — treat as repeated infringing [18.16], [19.4].
Escalate through game management actions as needed (advice → advance/escalate → warning → suspension → ordering off) [18.6].
rulings.notes: A player may ask an umpire to repeat a call or clarify where a sanction is taken — that is not a disputed ruling [19.5].
rulings.heading: Unfair play
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Incorrect team numbers
rulings.position: Possession to the opposing team where the ball was when play stopped (or the match is awarded if fewer than five players).
keyIndicators: Fewer than five players available (match awarded to opponents)
More than seven players on court (extra player sent off, possession awarded)
procedure: If a team has fewer than five players available at any time, award the match to the opposing team [3.2a].

If a team has more than seven on court, immediately send the additional player(s) off and award possession to the opposing team where the ball was when play stopped [3.2b]; penalise delay if they are slow to leave [19.1–19.2].
Signal possession with hand signal 6.
rulings.notes: One on-court player must always be the Centre [3.2].
rulings.heading: Members
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Incorrect entry — late player entering at the wrong time
rulings.position: The late player is sent from the court until the correct time for entry; possession is awarded to the opposing team where the ball was when play stopped.
keyIndicators: A late player takes the court other than at the next break in play after advising the umpire
A player who leaves the field of play without permission, or fails uniform/adornment checks during play [15.9], [4.4]
procedure: A late player may take a vacant position only at the next break in play, after advising the umpire [3.8].
If they enter at the wrong time, send them from the court until the correct time and award possession to the opposing team where the ball was when play stopped.
Terminology: 'Incorrect entry'. Signal possession with hand signal 6.
rulings.notes: Players failing [4.3] checks (uniform/adornment) during play are penalised as late players [4.4].
rulings.heading: Late players
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Failure to take the court
rulings.position: Penalise for delaying play [19.1–19.2] if the team takes the court within 30 seconds; otherwise award the match to the opposing team.
keyIndicators: A team does not have five players present at the start of a period of play
A team delays taking the court after a stoppage
procedure: If a team has fewer than five present at the start of a period, wait up to 30 seconds [3.6].
If they take the court within 30 seconds, start play and penalise for delaying play immediately after the whistle for the centre pass [3.6a], [19.1–19.2].
If not able to take the court within 30 seconds, award the match to the opposing team [3.6b].
If a team delays after a stoppage, penalise for delaying play as soon as play restarts [3.7].
rulings.notes: A team must take the court if at least five players are present, one of whom must be Centre [3.5].
rulings.heading: Failure to take the court
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Simultaneous / mutual infringement — award possession
rulings.position: Possession to the team who last had the ball immediately prior to the infringement, where the ball was when play stopped.
keyIndicators: Two opposing players gain possession, send the ball out, go offside, break, or contact each other simultaneously
Any mutual infringement where fault cannot be attributed to either team
procedure: For simultaneous or mutual infringements, award possession to the team who last had the ball immediately prior, where the ball was when play stopped [20.1], [6.16].
If both umpires blow simultaneously for opposing teams, the more significant sanction stands: foul play > major > minor/action; if equal, the controlling umpire's decision stands [20.4].
Signal possession with hand signal 6.
rulings.notes: If two opposing players enter an offside area or the centre third simultaneously and neither touches the ball, play on [20.2], [20.3].
rulings.heading: Procedure
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Possession — opposing players gain the ball in quick succession
rulings.position: Play continues; possession to the player who gained the ball first, who plays it.
keyIndicators: Two opposing players gain possession in quick succession (not simultaneously)
procedure: If two opposing players gain possession in quick succession, the umpire may allow play to continue by calling 'possession' and indicating the team and position of the player who gained it first [6.17].
The opposing player's hands must be removed quickly or they are penalised for contact [17.1].
Signal possession with hand signal 6.
rulings.notes: Contrast simultaneous possession [20.1a], where possession goes to the team who last had the ball.
rulings.heading: Possession
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Advantage — play on when a whistle would disadvantage the non-infringing team
rulings.terminology: Advantage (state the infringement and position of the infringer)
rulings.position: No stoppage — play continues.
keyIndicators: The non-infringing team has a clear and real opportunity to play the ball to a territorial and/or tactical advantage
procedure: Do not blow the whistle where doing so would disadvantage the non-infringing team; apply advantage and allow play to continue [7.1–7.2].
Call 'advantage', state the infringement and the infringer's position, and use hand signal 5.
If a goal is then scored to the non-infringing team's advantage, award the goal, calling 'advantage' and the infringement [7.5].
rulings.notes: Advantage must NOT be applied to unfair play, unsporting behaviour, dangerous play, any head/neck contact, or where a player may be seriously injured [7.4].
rulings.heading: Principles

rulings.title: Bench behaviour / bench movement
rulings.position: For behaviour [18.44]: penalty pass where the ball was when play stopped (no player stands out of play). For movement [18.43]: free pass.
keyIndicators: Team officials/bench players criticising umpires, using abusive language/gestures, excessive noise, encouraging foul play, or entering the court [18.44]
Bench players/officials off the team bench without a valid reason [18.43]
procedure: For prohibited bench behaviour, award a penalty pass to the non-infringing team where the ball was when play stopped; no player stands out of play [18.44]. Terminology: 'Bench behaviour'.
For bench movement without a valid reason, award a free pass [18.43]. Terminology: 'Bench movement'.
Either umpire may penalise; a warning may be issued to a person or all of that team's bench; persistent offenders are removed by the event organiser [18.45–18.47].
rulings.notes: If the ball was out of court, the pass is taken on court in line with where the ball was out.
rulings.heading: Discipline of team officials and bench players
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.

rulings.title: Stoppage for injury, illness or blood
rulings.terminology: Hold time (Incorrect stoppage procedures if breached)
rulings.position: Play restarts from where the ball was when play stopped (throw-in, sanction, or possession as applicable).
keyIndicators: A verifiable request for injury/illness, or an obvious/serious injury
Active bleeding, an open wound, or blood-stained clothing
procedure: Hold time (signal 2) for injury/illness on a verifiable request or an obvious/serious injury, or when you notice blood [10.5], [10.9], [10.12].
The player must leave the court within 30 seconds and be treated off court; timekeepers advise when 10 seconds remain [10.13]. Only primary care persons may come on to assess [10.14].
Both teams may make substitutions/team changes within the stoppage [10.19]. If no substitute, the position is left vacant; if the Centre, another player moves to Centre [10.20].
Restart from where the ball was: throw-in if out; the awarded sanction if one was signalled; or possession to the team that last had it [10.8].
rulings.notes: Breaching stoppage procedure is penalised with a free pass — 'Incorrect stoppage procedures' [10.7]. Blood on the ball → swap it; blood on court → clean as directed before restart [10.18].
rulings.heading: Injury/illness of a player or blood

rulings.title: Tactical change after a goal
rulings.position: No sanction — hold time briefly after a goal to allow the change.
keyIndicators: An on-court player requests to hold time for a substitution/team change immediately after a goal
procedure: After a goal, both teams may make tactical changes on a request from an on-court player to hold time [10.2]; use hand signal 12.
Ensure it is a tactical change (not injury/blood), players move without delay, officials stay at the bench, and play restarts quickly [10.2a–e].
If undue time is taken, penalise delaying play immediately after the whistle for the next centre pass [10.3]; frivolous/repeated requests may be refused [10.4].
rulings.notes: Substitutions/team changes are otherwise made only during an interval or an injury/illness/blood stoppage [10.1].
rulings.heading: Substitutions and team changes
Causing contact – player in the air
rulings.title: Causing contact — moving into the landing space of an airborne player
rulings.position: Penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless this disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the airborne player was standing).
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.
keyIndicators: A player who jumped from an on-court position must be allowed to land [17.4]
An opponent moves into that landing place, or fails to yield it to a player who gained possession in the air [17.5–17.6]
If safe landing is put at risk (e.g. head/neck), it is dangerous play and must be a game management action [17.9], [19.11]
procedure: A player who has jumped from an on-court position must be permitted to land, in the same place or another place on court [17.4].
Where opponents jump together, the one who gains possession has priority and must be allowed to land per the trajectory of the pass; others must yield [17.5].
An opponent must not move into that landing place or fail to yield it [17.6] — award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing and give hand signal 20.
If the action put safe landing at risk (especially head/neck contact), treat it as dangerous play: hold time and suspend (or order off in a serious case) [17.9], [19.11], [18.29].
rulings.notes: This is the rule behind the classic 'took the landing space' collision. If safety was endangered, the penalty pass is combined with a suspension/ordering off, not just a warning.
keywords: under the player in the air

rulings.heading: Conditions for throw-in
rulings.title: Preventing re-entry — blocking a player returning to court
rulings.position: Penalty pass on court near where the player left the court.
rulings.awardedTo: The non-infringing team — any player allowed in the area.
keyIndicators: A player who went out of court to retrieve a ball or take a throw-in is not allowed back on at the point where they left
procedure: A player who goes out of court to retrieve a ball or take a throw-in must be allowed back on at the point where they left or took the throw-in [6.10].
If an opponent prevents this re-entry, award a penalty pass on court near where the player left the court and give hand signal 10.
rulings.notes: Distinct from 'defending from out of court' [15.10] and 'leaving the court' [15.7].

rules.name: Technical specifications
rules.summary: Defines the court, its areas and the equipment.

sections.heading: Court and related areas
points: Rectangular, level and firm court: side lines 30.5 m (100 ft), goal lines 15.25 m (50 ft).
Two transverse lines divide the court into three equal thirds — a centre third and two goal thirds.
Centre circle 0.9 m (3 ft) diameter; a goal circle (semi-circle, radius 4.9 m / 16 ft) at each end.
All lines are 50 mm (2 in) wide and part of the area they bound; the court surround is 3.05 m (10 ft) wide.
During play only on-court players and umpires are allowed in the field of play; the bench zone is on one side.

sections.heading: Goalposts
points: A padded vertical pole 3.05 m (10 ft) high, set so it stays stable when knocked.
Ring of 380 mm (15 in) internal diameter on a 150 mm bar; net 380–457 mm long, open top and bottom.

sections.heading: Ball
points: Circumference 690–710 mm (27–28 in); weight 400–450 g (14–16 oz); inflated as marked by the manufacturer.
Match balls may be rotated during the match as set by the event organiser.

rules.name: Time
rules.summary: Match length, intervals and extra time.

sections.heading: Match length
points: Four quarters of 15 minutes; 4-minute intervals between 1st–2nd and 3rd–4th quarters; half-time 12 minutes (or 8 by agreement).
Teams change ends each quarter.
A period may be extended only for a penalty pass in the attacking goal circle awarded before the end signal.

sections.heading: Extra time
points: Used only if the event organiser sets it for a tie at full-time.
A 4-minute interval, then two halves of up to 7 minutes with a 1-minute half-time; teams change ends at half-time.
If still tied at the end, play continues until a team leads by two goals.

rules.name: Team
rules.summary: Players, playing positions, uniforms and team officials.

sections.heading: Members
points: Up to 12 players (maximum 7 on court at a time), one of whom must play Centre.
Fewer than five available players → the match is awarded to the opponents; more than seven on court → extra player off and possession to opponents ('Incorrect team numbers').

sections.heading: Failure to take the court
points: At the start of a period a team must field at least five players (one as Centre); umpires wait up to 30 seconds.
Taking the court within 30 s → penalised for delaying play; unable to → match awarded to the opponents.

sections.heading: Late players
points: A late player may take a vacant position only at the next break in play, after telling the umpire.
Entering at the wrong time → sent off until the correct time and possession to the opponents ('Incorrect entry').

sections.heading: Players
points: Registered uniform distinct from opponents, with position initials 150 mm (6 in) front and back; suitable non-spiked footwear.
No piercings, dangerous adornment or communication devices; medical/monitoring devices must be covered or secured; nails short; hair tied back.
Positions and permitted areas — GS 1,2 · GA 1,2,3 · WA 2,3 · C 2,3,4 · WD 3,4 · GD 3,4,5 · GK 4,5.
Captains toss for the first centre pass or goal end; a captain may seek rule clarification at an interval.

sections.heading: Team officials
points: Up to five officials including a coach and at least one primary care person (six only if a team doctor is used).
A primary care person may enter during a stoppage, or during play only in extreme circumstances where safety is endangered.

rules.name: Match officials
rules.summary: The two umpires and the reserve umpire.

sections.heading: Umpires
points: Two umpires control the match, each responsible for one half of the court including that goal line; they work co-operatively.
Before the match they check the court, goalposts, balls and players, and toss for goal end.
The whistle starts/ends play, restarts after a goal and signals infringements; out-of-court is whistled only when unclear.
Umpires move along the side line and behind the goal line, and may hold time for injury, blood, emergencies or foul play.

sections.heading: Reserve umpire
points: Replaces an ill or injured umpire, after learning any game-management action already taken.
Supervises suspended and ordered-off players and signals the centre-pass direction.

rules.name: Technical and event officials
rules.summary: Scorers, timekeepers and the event organiser.

sections.heading: Scorers
points: Keep an accurate score and record goals, unsuccessful shots, team changes and substitutions.
Keep a record of centre passes and confirm the correct centre pass on appeal.

sections.heading: Timekeepers
points: Time each period and interval and warn when 30 s and 10 s remain before a period starts.
Hold and restart time on the umpire's signal and time the suspension (2 min) and ordered-off (4 min) periods.

sections.heading: Event organiser
points: Prepares the enclosure, goalposts and balls, issues accreditation and arranges an independent concussion observer.
Decides emergency stoppages with the umpires and may abandon a match if safety is at risk.

rules.name: Sanctions and actions
rules.summary: Free pass, penalty pass, throw-in and possession — and how each is taken.

sections.heading: Types
points: Free pass for minor infringements; penalty pass for major infringements; throw-in for out-of-court; possession for simultaneous/mutual cases.
Taken where the infringement occurred (penalty: where the infringer stood, unless that disadvantages the non-infringing team).

sections.heading: Conditions for a free pass
points: No shot for goal may be taken directly from a free pass ('Shooting from free pass').

sections.heading: Conditions for a penalty pass
points: The infringer stands out of play beside the taker and takes no part — including comments — until the ball is released ('Participating').
A GS or GA taking a penalty pass in the goal circle may pass or shoot.

sections.heading: Conditions for a throw-in
points: Taken from outside the court with a foot within 15 cm (6 in) of the line at the indicated point; the ball must enter the court.
A player who left the court to retrieve the ball must be allowed back on where they left ('Preventing re-entry').

sections.heading: Possession
points: Awarded where the ball was when play stopped; for two opponents gaining it in quick succession, play may continue with whoever got it first.

sections.heading: Conditions for all sanctions and actions
points: Once set, the taker must obey the playing-the-ball, passing-distance and footwork rules; the placed foot counts as a one-foot landing.

sections.heading: Infringements during a break in play
points: Players must not infringe while the ball is out of play — before a throw-in, after a goal, during a stoppage, or before a sanction is taken.

rules.name: Advantage
rules.summary: Playing on when a whistle would disadvantage the non-infringing team.

sections.heading: Principles
points: The umpire withholds the whistle where blowing it would disadvantage the non-infringing team, calling 'advantage' with the infringement and infringer.
Advantage may be territorial, tactical, or both.

sections.heading: Not to be applied
points: Never applied to unfair play, unsporting behaviour, dangerous play, any head/neck contact, or a possible serious injury.

sections.heading: If a goal is scored
points: If a goal is then scored to the non-infringing team's advantage, the umpire awards it.

rules.name: Centre pass
rules.summary: Starting and restarting play with the centre pass.

sections.heading: Principles
points: Centre passes alternate between the two Centres; both umpires check the correct centre pass with the scorers.

sections.heading: Position of players
points: The passing Centre stands with at least one foot wholly in the centre circle; the opposing Centre is in the centre third.
All other players must be in their correct thirds; only the two Centres may be in the centre third before the whistle ('Breaking').

sections.heading: Controlling the centre pass
points: After the whistle the Centre may step out but must obey footwork and release within three seconds ('Held ball').
The pass must be caught or touched by a player standing in, or landing first/both feet in, the centre third ('Untouched').

rules.name: Scoring a goal
rules.summary: How a goal is scored and the rules for taking a shot.

sections.heading: Requirements
points: A goal is scored when the ball passes completely through the ring from a shot by GS or GA inside the goal circle (including the bounding lines).
A defender's deflection that still goes through counts; a shot completed after the end/hold-time whistle can still score.

sections.heading: Taking a shot
points: The shooter must have no ground contact outside the goal circle ('Incorrect shot'), shoot within three seconds, and obey footwork.
A defender may not move the post or deflect a shot on its downward flight, including up through the net ('Interference with shot').

rules.name: Stoppages
rules.summary: Substitutions, team changes, injury/illness, blood and emergencies.

sections.heading: Substitutions and team changes
points: Allowed during an interval or a stoppage for injury/illness/blood; unlimited, using named players.
Tactical changes may be made after a goal by holding time, provided play restarts quickly; frivolous requests may be refused.

sections.heading: Procedures
points: Umpires must hold time for injury/illness on a verifiable request or an obvious injury, and when they notice blood.
Play restarts from where the ball was — a throw-in, the awarded sanction, or possession to the team that last had it.

sections.heading: Injury/illness of a player or blood
points: The player leaves the court within 30 seconds (a 10-second warning is given); only primary care persons may come on to assess.
Blood on the ball → swap it; blood on court → clean before restart; a vacant position may be refilled at the next break in play.

sections.heading: Emergencies
points: Umpires may hold time or extend an interval for serious injury, an official's illness, court/equipment/weather issues, or other extreme circumstances.

rules.name: Playing the ball
rules.summary: Gaining and keeping possession, and prohibited ways of playing the ball.

sections.heading: Gaining possession
points: Catch; roll to oneself; catch a rebound off the post; bat once then catch; bounce once then catch; or touch in an uncontrolled manner then catch.

sections.heading: While in possession
points: Pass or shoot within three seconds ('Held ball').
After releasing the ball, do not touch it again before another player or a rebound off the post ('Repossession').

sections.heading: Without having possession
points: May bat once, or bounce once, then bat or bounce the ball to another player — exceeding this is a 'Replayed ball'.

sections.heading: Prohibited actions
points: No falling on the ball or playing it while lying/sitting/kneeling; no using the goalpost as a support.
No kicking, striking with a fist, or rolling the ball to another player.

rules.name: Passing distances
rules.summary: The short pass and the over-a-third rules.

sections.heading: Short pass
points: There must be room for an opponent to contest the ball as it travels from passer to receiver; too close is a 'Short pass'.

sections.heading: Over a third
points: The ball must be caught or touched by a player in each third; it may not travel over a whole third untouched ('Over a third').
A player astride the transverse line must have their pass taken in one of those two thirds.

rules.name: Footwork
rules.summary: Legal footwork for one-foot and two-foot landings.

sections.heading: One-foot landing
points: The landing foot may be lifted but the ball must be released before it is regrounded; the other foot may step, or the player may pivot on the landing foot.

sections.heading: Two-foot landing
points: Either foot may be chosen as the landing foot; step or pivot but release before regrounding the lifted foot.

sections.heading: Other foot movements
points: No dragging or sliding the landing foot, hopping, or jumping from and landing on both feet while still holding the ball.

rules.name: Offside
rules.summary: Entering an area not designated for your position.

sections.heading: Requirements
points: A player is offside on entering an area not allowed for their position, with or without the ball.
Not offside if a body part is on (not over) their own line, or when reaching in without grounding in that area.
Of two opponents entering offside, the first is penalised; if simultaneous and neither touches the ball, play continues.

rules.name: Out of court
rules.summary: Ball and players in relation to the court boundary.

sections.heading: Ball out of court
points: Out when it touches the ground, an object or a person outside the court; throw-in to the team that did not last touch it.
Not out if it rebounds off the post into court, or lands on (not over) a line.

sections.heading: Player outside the court
points: A player is out if they catch or hold the ball while touching the ground outside the court; they may jump from inside and pass/shoot before landing outside.
Leaving the court to gain an advantage is penalised ('Leaving the court').

sections.heading: Defending from out of court
points: A player standing outside the court may not defend an on-court player ('Defending from out of court').

rules.name: Obstruction
rules.summary: Defending distance and use of the arms.

sections.heading: Player in possession of the ball
points: A defender must be at least 0.9 m (3 ft) — measured on the ground from the landing foot — before attempting to defend, intercept or deflect.
Adjust when the ball-carrier pivots; a defender within 0.9 m may stand still while making no attempt to defend.

sections.heading: Player not in possession of the ball
points: Within 0.9 m a player may reach to catch/deflect/intercept a pass or rebound, or briefly signal — but not use arm movements to prevent an opponent's movement.

rules.name: Contact
rules.summary: Fair contest versus penalised contact, and causing contact.

sections.heading: Interference
points: Physical contact that unfairly interferes with an opponent — pushing, holding, hitting the ball in their hands, etc. — is penalised; incidental contact that does not interfere is fair contest.

sections.heading: Causing contact – player in the air
points: A player who jumps must be allowed to land; an opponent must not move into, or fail to yield, that landing space.

sections.heading: Causing contact – moving player
points: A player must not move so late or so close into a moving opponent's path that they cannot stop or change direction.

sections.heading: Inevitable contact
points: Players must not position so close that an opponent cannot move at all without making contact.

sections.heading: Contact endangering player safety
points: Actions that put a safe landing at risk, or cause head/neck contact, are treated as dangerous play.

rules.name: Game management
rules.summary: How umpires manage behaviour and discipline.

sections.heading: Principles
points: Umpires apply the rules fairly and calmly, must not coach or criticise players, and treat player safety as paramount; any foul play receives the appropriate action.

sections.heading: Game management actions
points: In escalating order: proactive advice; advance and/or escalate a sanction; warning; suspension (2 minutes); ordering off (4 minutes, no return).

sections.heading: Proactive advice
points: Brief feedback to change low-level behaviour without holding time; needing to repeat it becomes repeated infringing.

sections.heading: Advance and/or escalate a sanction
points: A sanction may be advanced up to half a third (into the goal circle if the infringement was in the goal third) and/or a free pass escalated to a penalty pass.

sections.heading: Warning
points: Given when behaviour does not change and for unfair play, and always for unsporting behaviour; only one warning per player in a match.

sections.heading: Suspension
points: Two minutes' playing time off court; required for dangerous play unless serious enough to order off; only one per player.

sections.heading: Ordering off
points: The player takes no further part; required for intentional or highly reckless dangerous play; a substitute may enter after four minutes.

sections.heading: Discipline of team officials and bench players
points: They must stay at the bench and must not criticise umpires, use abuse, or enter the court ('Bench behaviour' / 'Bench movement'); persistent offenders are removed by the event organiser.

rules.name: Foul play
rules.summary: Unfair play, unsporting behaviour and dangerous play.

sections.heading: Unfair play
points: Delaying play, intentional or repeated infringing, disputing a ruling, or intimidation — penalty pass which is advanced.

sections.heading: Unsporting behaviour
points: Retaliation, abuse, or actions against good sporting behaviour — penalty pass and at least a warning; ordering off in a serious case.

sections.heading: Dangerous play
points: Any forceful, careless, reckless or dangerous action affecting safety (especially head/neck) — penalty pass and suspension, or ordering off for intentional or highly reckless acts.

rules.name: Simultaneous and mutual infringements
rules.summary: Deciding outcomes when fault cannot be separated.

sections.heading: Procedure
points: Possession goes to the team that last had the ball before the infringement.
Simultaneous offside/breaking with no touch → play on; if both umpires whistle together for opposing teams, the more significant sanction stands (foul play > major > minor/action).

rules.name: Variations for other levels of play
rules.summary: Permitted variations for non-international play.

sections.heading: Principles
points: The rules are written for international play; variations may be made for other levels while keeping the game's integrity, decided by the competition's controlling authority.

sections.heading: Examples of variations
points: Outdoor courts and lower-grade (2-ply) balls; a lower goalpost or a smaller ball for young children.
Time may be played in halves (up to 20 minutes) with shorter intervals; teams may be mixed; fewer technical officials may be appointed.

gameManagement.name: Game management
gameManagement.heading: Game management actions
gameManagement.intro: For any repeated or ongoing infringing, the umpire works through the game-management actions in order, unless an act is serious enough to jump straight to a higher level. Player safety is the paramount consideration.

ladder.label: Proactive advice
ladder.desc: Specific feedback to the player to change their behaviour, without holding time.

ladder.label: Advance and/or escalate the sanction
ladder.desc: Advance the sanction up to half a third (into the goal circle if the infringement was in the goal third) and/or escalate a free pass to a penalty pass.

ladder.label: Warning
ladder.desc: Formally warn the player that suspension will follow if they keep infringing the foul-play rules. Only one warning per player in a match.

ladder.label: Suspension
ladder.desc: The player takes no part in play for two minutes' playing time. Only one suspension per player.

ladder.label: Ordering off
ladder.desc: The player takes no further part in the match; the team may replace them after four minutes' playing time.

gameManagement.notes: Repeated infringing after being spoken to is itself unfair play [19.4], [18.16]. Advancing/escalating is not usually used for infringements that endanger safety — those go straight to suspension or ordering off [18.20].

dangerous-play-severity.prompt: This affects player safety, so the game-management action depends on your judgement. How do you grade the action?
dangerous-play-severity.safety: Hold time immediately for the injury; the player leaves the court within 30 seconds for assessment [10.13]. Advantage must never be applied to dangerous play or any head/neck contact [7.4].
factors: Was the action intentional, reckless or avoidable? [19.12]
Low or high impact on player safety?
Low or high speed — on the ground or in the air?
Was the player stationary or moving?

result.detail: A player must always be ordered off for intentional or highly reckless acts of dangerous play. The player takes no further part in the match; the team may replace them after four minutes' playing time. Award a penalty pass to the non-infringing team where the infringer was standing (unless that disadvantages them, then where the airborne player was).

Dangerous play must be at least a suspension — two minutes' playing time off court, with the position left vacant (unless the player is Centre). Award a penalty pass to the non-infringing team where the infringer was standing (unless that disadvantages them, then where the airborne player was).

If safety was not endangered, penalise 'Causing contact' with a penalty pass where the infringer was standing; apply normal game management (advice, advance/escalate, warning) only if the behaviour repeats. Note: moving into an opponent's landing space still causes contact, so a penalty pass applies.

contact-interference.prompt: Contact is only penalised if it actually interfered with the opponent. Did it?
factors: Did it cause the opponent to lose the ball? [17.2a]
Did it interfere with a passing or shooting action? [17.2b]
Did it change the opponent's body position and unfairly disadvantage them? [17.2c]

result.detail: Award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless that disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the contacted player was). The infringer stands out of play until the ball is released.
Incidental contact that does not cause interference is deemed fair contest and is not penalised. Play continues.
Treat as dangerous play: hold time, award a penalty pass and apply a game-management action (suspend, or order off for intentional/highly reckless acts). Use the dangerous-play judgement to grade it.

obstruction-attempt.prompt: Within 0.9 m (3 ft), obstruction only applies if the defender attempts to defend or interferes. What happened?
factors: Was the defender less than 0.9 m from the landing foot of the player with the ball? [16.1]
Did they attempt to defend, intercept or deflect, or interfere with the passing/shooting action? [16.7]
Or were they simply standing with no defending effort? [16.7]

result.detail: Award a penalty pass where the infringer was standing (unless that disadvantages the non-infringing team, then where the obstructed player was). The infringer stands out of play until the ball is released.
A defender within 0.9 m who makes no attempt to defend and does not interfere with the passing or shooting action is not obstructing. Play continues.
If the nearer foot was 0.9 m (3 ft) or more from the landing foot, the defender is at a legal distance and may defend. Play continues.

advantage-or-whistle.prompt: An opponent has infringed. Would blowing the whistle disadvantage the non-infringing team — do they have a clear, real chance to play the ball to their advantage?
advantage-or-whistle.safety: Advantage must NEVER be applied to unfair play, unsporting behaviour, dangerous play, any head/neck contact, or where a player may be seriously injured [7.4]. In those cases, always blow.
factors: Does the non-infringing team have possession or a clear chance to gain it? [7.2]
Is there a territorial and/or tactical advantage to be gained? [7.2]
Where are the other players — is the advantage real, not just possible?

result.detail: Do not blow. Call 'advantage', state the infringement and the infringer's position, and use hand signal 5. If a goal is then scored to the non-infringing team's advantage, award it [7.5].

result.action: Blow the whistle and award the sanction
result.detail: Penalise the infringement with its normal sanction where it occurred. When in doubt, or for any foul play, blow the whistle.
